independence: Money Intelligence only; no signal-engine or broker state changed.
observed_facts: Federal Reserve H.4.1 released 2026-09-17 shows Wednesday Sep. 16 TGA at $991.708B, up $148.003B from Sep. 9, while Wednesday depository-institution reserve balances were $2.921537T, down $114.971B. Fed securities held outright rose only $2.051B over the same Wednesday-to-Wednesday interval.
The H.4.1 weekly-average figures are less dramatic: average TGA $877.028B and average reserves $3.013794T, so point-in-time settlement/tax-date mechanics matter materially.

The BOJ raised its policy rate 25 bp to 1.25% on Sep. 18, but the yen weakened; Reuters reported USD/JPY around 158.07, up more than 1.2%, as markets focused on two dissenters and insufficiently hawkish guidance.
Reuters Sep. 18 reported Brent around $103-$104 as Saudi rerouting, product-inventory builds and Chinese refined-product exports reduced immediate supply-scarcity fears.

Reuters Sep. 18 fund-flow reporting showed global equity funds lost $23.21B in the week ended Sep. 16, the largest weekly outflow in nine months; U.S. equity funds lost $31.44B while Asian equity funds received $6.26B and sector funds received $4.49B, led by technology, financials and consumer discretionary.
inferences: The pre-event TGA-rebuild mechanism was directionally validated at the balance-sheet level: Treasury cash accumulation coincided with a large reserve drain while Fed assets were nearly unchanged. This is not evidence by itself of funding stress or a risk-asset sell signal.

The Sep. 15-16 episode is a high-information test of the prior claim that sub-10%-of-GDP Fed liquidity is a sensitivity regime rather than a mechanical scarcity trigger. Final classification requires transaction-based SOFR/TGCR distributions and standing-repo usage for the event dates.

BOJ Sep. 18 is a fresh matched case supporting the expectation-adjusted-policy-surprise hypothesis: the sign of the action was hawkish, but the yen moved in the opposite direction because the hike was expected and guidance/vote composition changed the inferred future path.
Cross-asset flows remain selective rather than uniformly risk-off: aggregate U.S./global equity outflows coexist with sector-level technology inflows and Asian equity inflows.

hypotheses.claim: Large tax/settlement-driven TGA rebuilds can drain reserves materially without causing broad funding stress when private repo intermediation and Fed backstops retain capacity.
hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Retrieve Sep. 15-17 SOFR/TGCR median and upper-percentile spreads to IORB, EFFR-IORB, and standing-repo take-up; compare with pre-event baseline.

hypotheses.claim: For central-bank FX reactions, the expectation-adjusted future path and vote/guidance surprise dominate the sign of a fully anticipated rate hike.
hypotheses.next_falsification_test: Add BOJ Sep. 18 as a matched event to the planned historical central-bank sample and compare pre-event pricing with 30m/1d/5d FX and rates responses.

big_move_lab_candidates.mechanism: expected hike -> little positive rate surprise -> two dissents / insufficiently hawkish guidance -> shallower inferred future tightening path -> yen selling / USDJPY rise

decision_support: WAIT / NO NEW TRADE THESIS. The strongest new evidence improves causal understanding of Treasury-liquidity transmission and expectation-relative central-bank pricing but does not yet clear the canonical actionability bar.
next_priority: Resolve the Sep. 15 funding-stress test with event-date repo distributions and standing-repo usage before changing the canonical dashboard or promoting the TGA mechanism from conditional sensitivity to realized funding stress/no-stress.
